Our Vision and Values
Our vision is to ensure that our students gain the knowledge and experience they need, and the strength of character to become changemakers in the world, living well and improving the lives of others. We achieve this by:
Our values
Everything we do is based on our core values of:
Social justice
Kindness and empathy
Endeavour
Community
Our motto
‘Create a better future’
Being influenced by our values empowers us to make an impact in our own lives and in the life of the community.
What makes us different?
Our unique Pathways programme takes students on an inspirational journey beyond the National Curriculum, opening their eyes through new experiences, dynamic projects, and positive engagement with organisations from a wide range of sectors. This enhances students’ employability skills, preparing them for high value academic, professional, and technical careers.
Our offer includes an after school and holiday programme, bespoke mentoring and tutoring, extensive advice and guidance, a guest speaker programme, and interesting workplace visits. High-spec facilities and equipment are provided including a Chromebook of their own during students’ time in school.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results Day 2026: Year 11s ready for what comes next
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results Day 2026: Year 11s ready for what comes next
Published: 20 August 2026
South Bank University Academy is celebrating its Year 11 students today as the Class of 2026 receive their GCSE results and take their next steps towards sixth form, further education and their future careers.
Results Day marks a significant milestone for young people after five years of secondary education. Today, students returned to SBUA to collect their results, celebrate with friends and teachers, and begin looking ahead to what comes next.
Across the Academy, students have been celebrating their individual achievements, with strong results in English and Mathematics and a wide range of exciting post-16 destinations secured.
Celebrating GCSE achievement
Among this year's results highlights:
The Academy is proud to celebrate the individual successes behind these figures, recognising that every student's journey through secondary education is different.
For many students, today's results reflect years of hard work, perseverance and determination. For others, they represent significant personal progress and the achievement of goals they have worked towards throughout their time at SBUA.
Every student has a story
While today's results provide an important snapshot of achievement, Results Day is ultimately about celebrating the young people behind the grades.
Students across the year group have been sharing their results, reflecting on their time at SBUA and looking forward to their next steps.
Santiago is celebrating an impressive set of GCSE results, achieving two Grade 8s in English Language and History, three Grade 7s in Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics, three Grade 6s in English Literature, Biology and Sociology, and a Grade 5 in Spanish.
After feeling nervous throughout the morning as he waited to receive his results, Santiago was delighted when he finally opened them.
“I was very nervous this morning about getting my results, but now that I've got them, I'm very happy with them.”
Santiago will now continue his studies at Haberdashers' Borough Academy Sixth Form, taking the next step towards his future ambitions.
Joanne is also celebrating a strong set of results, including an outstanding Grade 9 in Mathematics, Grade 8s in Chemistry and Physics, Grade 7s in Biology and English Language, a Grade 6 in English Literature, a Grade 5 in Drama and a Grade 4 in Art.
Joanne said she is “happy and proud” of her results and is looking forward to continuing her education at South Bank University Academy Sixth Form.
For Joanne, Results Day marks not only the celebration of her GCSE achievements, but also the beginning of the next stage of her journey within the SBUA community.
These stories represent just some of the many individual achievements being celebrated across the Class of 2026.
A cohort demonstrating resilience
The Class of 2026 is a diverse cohort, with students bringing a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, strengths and aspirations to the Academy.
The year group includes a higher proportion of students with special educational needs and disabilities than both the school and national averages. Attendance was also a significant challenge for the cohort during their secondary education, despite targeted interventions and support from the Academy and external partners.
Against this backdrop, the achievements of students today are a reflection not only of their academic attainment, but also of their resilience, determination and the support they have received throughout their secondary education.
Teachers and support staff have worked closely with students and families to help them overcome barriers, develop confidence and remain focused on their future goals.
Today provides an opportunity to recognise that work and, most importantly, to celebrate the students themselves.
Continuing the journey at SBUA
For many members of the Class of 2026, today's GCSE results are not the end of their SBUA journey, but the beginning of an exciting new chapter.
A significant number of students will be returning to South Bank University Academy Sixth Form, continuing their education within the SBUA community and building on the foundations they have developed during their secondary education.
The Academy is also welcoming a new group of external Year 11 students today who are joining SBUA for sixth form enrolment, making Results Day a particularly exciting occasion across the school as one cohort prepares to move forward while another begins its journey.
For students progressing elsewhere, the next chapter will take them to a range of destinations, including South Bank Colleges, part of the LSBU Group, alongside other sixth forms, colleges and post-16 pathways.
Whatever destination they have chosen, each student is taking the next step towards their individual ambitions and future careers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Black History Month: Honouring Our Communities
pageCache.text:
Black History Month: Honouring Our Communities
Published: 02 October 2026
SBUA came together today for a whole-school assembly to mark Black History Month, led by our Head Boy, Promise, alongside members of the Black History Month Student Leadership Team.
We were delighted to welcome Sadiq (Sid) Adebiyi and Neil Tchamambe from the London Broncos, who joined students to share their experiences and talk about their journeys.
Students had the opportunity to hear from both players before taking part in a Q&A. The questions covered a wide range of topics, including their GCSEs, A Levels, university, qualifications and the steps they took to build their careers.
The conversation clearly struck a chord with students. Several stayed behind after the assembly to continue speaking with Sid and Neil, asking further questions about their experiences and how they had reached where they are today.
It was a valuable opportunity for students to listen, learn and engage directly with people whose experiences could help them think about their own futures.
A big thank you to Sid and Neil for taking the time to speak with our students, and to Promise and the Black History Month Student Leadership Team for leading the assembly.

pageCache.text:
Business Networking Event Creates New Opportunities for Students
Published: 20 July 2026
Earlier this month, SBUA was delighted to host a Business Networking Event designed to strengthen existing partnerships and establish exciting new connections with organisations across a range of sectors.
The event brought together representatives from the private sector, the Civil Service and London South Bank University (LSBU), providing an excellent opportunity to share our vision for the future and showcase the exciting developments taking place across the Academy. Guests heard about our expanded Key Stage 5 curriculum offer for next year, with particular interest in the introduction of three new T Level pathways, which will provide students with valuable industry-focused learning opportunities and stronger routes into higher education and employment.
A key focus of the meeting was exploring how meaningful partnerships can be developed to benefit both SBUA students and our partner organisations. Discussions were highly positive and productive, generating a range of ideas for future collaboration, including employer engagement activities, work experience opportunities, industry insight events and skills development initiatives.
Visitors were also given an exclusive tour of the Academy’s new Digital Hub. The first phase of this exciting facility will open in September and will feature an immersive Virtual Reality teaching room, a dedicated podcast studio and a green-screen production room. The new Hub generated considerable enthusiasm among attendees, highlighting the innovative learning experiences that will soon be available to our students.
The event was a great success, reinforcing the strong relationships we have already built while creating new opportunities for collaboration in the future. We would like to thank all those who attended and contributed to such engaging and constructive discussions. We look forward to welcoming even more partners to future networking events in the new academic year as we continue to work together to support and inspire our students.

Future Pathways Programme Launches for 2026-27
Published: 23 September 2026
This week saw the first Future Pathways Programme (FPP) Day of the academic year at SBUA. The Future Pathways Programme is a key part of our commitment to ensuring every student is equipped with the knowledge, skills, experiences and aspirations needed to succeed in education, employment and beyond. Through a carefully planned programme of activities, workshops and employer and university engagement, students are supported to make informed decisions about their future pathways.
Future Pathway Programmes
Sixth form
Year 11 and Year 12: Launching Unifrog
Students in Years 11 and 12 began the day with the launch of Unifrog, an innovative online platform that helps young people explore future opportunities, research careers, and make informed choices about their next steps.
Year 11 students then took part in a carousel of workshops designed to develop key life and study skills. Sessions included:
Meanwhile, Year 12 students visited London South Bank University (LSBU) to deepen their understanding of higher education opportunities and the benefits of being part of the South Bank group. During the visit, students:
The visit provided valuable insight into university study and helped students begin thinking about their future aspirations and progression routes.
Personal finance and money management skills.
Year 13: Preparing for the Future
Year 13 students focused on preparing for life beyond sixth form. The day began with a presentation from members of the LSBU Admissions Team, who shared expert advice on creating a strong UCAS application and what makes an outstanding personal statement that helps applicants stand out from the crowd.
Students then participated in a Study Foundations and AI for Learning workshop delivered by Elevate Education UK, providing practical strategies to maximise academic success during this crucial year.
The remainder of the morning was dedicated to refining UCAS applications and updating CVs, ensuring students are well prepared for the next stage of their journey.
Gardening, Biodiversity and Wellbeing
Our well-established Gardening Club also had a productive day, leading work on the new planters around the school. This follows our successful funding bid to increase biodiversity across the site. Students put into practice knowledge gained from specialist workshops delivered last year by the Worshipful Company of Gardeners and the Royal Horticultural Society, helping to create a greener and more vibrant environment for everyone in our school community.
Ending the Day with Sport
The day concluded with a range of sporting activities, giving students the opportunity to develop teamwork, resilience and wellbeing. Activities included:
The energy, enthusiasm and sportsmanship displayed throughout the afternoon were fantastic to see.
Basketball tournament
Football tournament
Badminton
Student Voice
“The LSBU visit helped me understand what university is really like. Speaking to students and staff gave me confidence about my future and helped me start thinking seriously about my options.”Year 12 Student
“I learned so much throughout the day, especially about using AI effectively for studying and managing my personal finances. It felt really useful because everything linked directly to our future goals.”Year 11 Student
Looking Ahead
The first Future Pathways Programme Day was a fantastic success, providing students with meaningful experiences, practical skills and valuable opportunities to plan for their futures.
We are already looking forward to our next Future Pathways Programme Day on Tuesday 2nd December, where students will continue developing the knowledge, confidence and aspirations needed for success beyond SBUA.

pageCache.pageTitle: Results Day 2026: Celebrating achievement, progress and our best-ever vocational results
pageCache.text:
Results Day 2026: Celebrating achievement, progress and our best-ever vocational results
Published: 13 August 2026
Today marks an important moment for the SBUA Class of 2026 as students celebrate their results and the progress they have made throughout their educational journey.
Results Day is a chance to recognise more than grades. It is a moment to celebrate the commitment, resilience and determination that students have shown throughout their studies, while looking ahead to the opportunities that come next.
This year, SBUA is celebrating its best-ever vocational results, with students achieving strong outcomes across a range of subjects.
Across vocational qualifications:
35% of students achieved DDD or above
77% of students achieved MMM or above
There were particularly strong outcomes in Digital Media, where 57% of students achieved DDD or above and 100% achieved MMM or above. On average, Digital Media students achieved three grades higher than expected, demonstrating significant progress against their expected attainment.
Business students also performed strongly, achieving an average of one full grade higher than expected.
Strong A Level outcomes were also achieved in Design & Technology, with 50% of students achieving A or A grades*. In Mathematics, 40% of students achieved A or A grades*.
Sixth form
Exceptional individual achievements
Among the individual successes this year, Favour, a Digital Media student, achieved an outstanding D*D*D*, known as a Triple Distinction Star.*
For Favour, the result was particularly meaningful because it was exactly what she had hoped for when she began Year 12.
“These were the grades I wanted from the very first day I started Year 12, so I’m really proud to have achieved them. Twenty One Pilots was also a big influence on me and my creativity.”
Her Digital Media studies were a particular highlight, and she credits the support of her teacher with helping her achieve her results.
“I felt really supported by my Media teacher. She helped me so much throughout the course and really pushed me to achieve these grades.”
Favour will now continue her creative journey at UAL, taking the next step towards her future studies and career.
Her advice to younger students is simple:
“Just keep working hard.”
A journey of progress and determination
Results Day is also a chance to recognise the progress students have made from their starting points.
Hanan achieved DMM in Digital Media, exceeding her target grades. Her reaction to receiving her results was immediate:
“I’m so happy! I worked really hard for these results, so it feels amazing to see it pay off.”
Hanan will now continue her studies at London South Bank University (LSBU), part of the wider LSBU Group, taking her next step in education.
Her brother, Abdullahi, achieved DMM in Digital Media, also exceeding his target grades.
The siblings joined SBUA in Year 9 with limited to no English. Since then, they have worked hard to develop their English language skills, build confidence and make sustained progress throughout their education.
Reflecting on how far he has come, Abdullahi said:
“When I joined SBUA, I could barely speak or understand English. I’m really proud of what I’ve achieved in the time I’ve had.”
His results are a powerful example of the progress that can be achieved through determination, resilience and hard work.
Together, Hanan and Abdullahi's results represent not only strong vocational attainment, but a remarkable educational journey.
Celebrating progress and different pathways
At SBUA, students follow a range of academic and vocational pathways, reflecting their individual strengths, interests and aspirations.
Results Day provides an opportunity to recognise every student's starting point and the progress they have made. For some, today's results will lead to university. For others, the next step may be an apprenticeship, employment, further education or another form of training.
The strong vocational outcomes this year highlight the value of providing students with opportunities to develop practical, creative and industry-relevant skills alongside their academic education.
The results in Digital Media and Business, alongside the strong A Level outcomes in Design & Technology and Mathematics, demonstrate the breadth of achievement across the sixth form.
“Well done to the fantastic SBUA students. Their hard work, commitment and determination, together with the unwavering support and dedication of SBUA teachers and support staff, have contributed to these wonderful achievements. Students have taken an inspiring first step towards creating bright and successful futures, and we wish them every success as they continue into this exciting next chapter. We look forward to celebrating many more of their achievements in the years ahead.”
- Principal, Mrs Annette Moses
Behind every result is a student, a journey and a great deal of hard work.
Today, the focus is on celebrating those achievements and looking ahead to what comes next.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026.
You did it. We did it.
We look forward to seeing the next chapter of each student's journey and celebrating many more achievements in the years ahead.

pageCache.pageTitle: SBUA Rugby Players Continue to Make Their Mark
pageCache.text:
SBUA Rugby Players Continue to Make Their Mark
Published: 16 September 2026
Four SBUA rugby league players have enjoyed an exciting summer of rugby, with a series of achievements highlighting the strength of their development and the opportunities available through their sporting pathways.
On Bank Holiday Monday, 31 August, three SBUA students proudly represented London Broncos U16s at the Halliwell Jones Stadium in Warrington, as part of the build-up to the 1895 Cup Final.
Playing in front of around 5,000 spectators, the Broncos faced a strong Widnes U16 side in a closely contested match. Although the team narrowly missed out on the win, the experience provided the students with an invaluable insight into the demands and atmosphere of a professional matchday.
From travelling and preparing with the team to running out at a major stadium and playing in front of a large crowd, the students experienced first-hand what life as an elite athlete can look like.
The day became even more memorable when, following London Broncos' dramatic success in the 1895 Cup Final, the students were invited onto the pitch to celebrate alongside the first-team squad and pose with the trophy.
More opportunities ahead
The three London Broncos representatives, alongside a fourth SBUA rugby league player, have also been selected to represent South London in this year's North v South representative fixtures.
This is a fantastic achievement, particularly as all four students are still U15s and will be competing against players from across the region who are a year older.
There is also individual recognition for Yiska, who has been shortlisted for the prestigious London Junior League Player of the Year Award. The winner will be announced at Plough Lane Stadium following the first North v South representative fixture.
Yiska's nomination is a fantastic achievement and reflects the progress he has made both individually and as a young player.
Congratulations to all four students on their achievements so far. Their commitment, hard work and performances continue to be a credit to themselves, their families and SBUA.

pageCache.text:
Year 10 Students Inspired by Marketing Industry Leader
Published: 10 July 2026
Year 10 students recently welcomed Bryan, Chief Marketing Officer at Ozone, for an engaging careers workshop exploring the world of marketing and the skills needed to build a successful career.
Drawing on his own professional journey, Bryan shared how his career has evolved, the experiences that have shaped him and the opportunities available within the marketing industry. Students gained valuable insight into what it is like to work in a senior leadership role, while learning that career paths are rarely linear and are often shaped by embracing new opportunities and experiences.
A key focus of the session was personal branding and the importance of learning how to market yourself. Bryan encouraged students to think about how they present their strengths, communicate their skills and build confidence, highlighting how these qualities can help them stand out when applying for further education, apprenticeships and future employment.
The workshop concluded with an interactive Q&A, where students asked thoughtful questions about Bryan's career, the challenges he has faced and the advice he would give to his younger self. His honest reflections encouraged students to remain curious, stay open to opportunities and recognise that success often comes from continuous learning and personal growth.
One Year 10 student reflected on the session, saying:
"It was a very interesting session. Usually I find it hard to focus for a long time, but I did during this session. Bryan taught us where they started from and where they are now. My main takeaway was that we are not limited to any job but can be anything we desire."
Experiences like this form an important part of SBUA's Future Pathways Programme, giving students the opportunity to hear directly from industry professionals and helping them make informed decisions about their future pathways.
We would like to thank Bryan and Ozone for generously sharing their time, experience and expertise with our students. Their insights have inspired students to think more confidently about their future careers and the opportunities available to them.

pageCache.text:
Macmillan Coffee Morning Brings the SBUA Community Together
Published: 25 September 2026
SBUA was full of coffee, homemade treats and good conversation this morning as students and staff came together for a Macmillan Coffee Morning.
The event gave the school community an opportunity to support Macmillan Cancer Support while enjoying a relaxed start to the day.
A special highlight was seeing our Year 12 students take the lead in organising and running the event. They were involved from start to finish, helping to prepare the food, set up the space, welcome staff and keep everything running throughout the morning.
It was a great opportunity for students to put their organisation, teamwork and communication skills into practice, while taking an active role in bringing the wider school community together.
Thank you to everyone who baked, donated, bought something or stopped by to support the morning. Your contributions helped make the event a lovely success.
A big well done to the Year 12 students for taking the initiative and making the Macmillan Coffee Morning happen. 💚

Career Pathways
At South Bank University Academy, we provide a clear and supported pathway from secondary education to further study or the world of work. Our approach ensures that every student’s aspirations are prioritised, with progression into further education, apprenticeships or employment at the heart of everything we do.
Through our structured Careers Programme, students receive personalised guidance, access to up-to-date labour market information and meaningful experiences that connect classroom learning to the world beyond school. We want every student to understand how their subjects link to real careers and to feel empowered to pursue pathways that reflect their interests, strengths and ambitions.
Our approach is rooted in opportunity, aspiration and achievement. By exposing students to a variety of sectors and progression routes, we help them build the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to succeed in their chosen field.
Browse our Career Pathways
Click on a pathway below to explore different careers, learn about each sector and discover the steps to get there.
Applied Science and Dental
If you have a passion for problem solving and a great eye for detail, a career in applied science and dental could be ideal for you. The life sciences directly employ over 250,000 people across the UK in more than 6,500 businesses. Careers range from lab-based clinical research to sport and exercise science and there are thousands of exciting opportunities within the sector. Science is continually evolving so you will be working at the forefront of the very latest breakthroughs and discoveries.
Find out more about Applied Science and Dental careers
Built Environment, Construction and Green Energy
Every building and structure that we create is brought to life by skilled and practical professionals with the vision and capability to realise amazing projects. Whether you are inspired by the practical aspects of construction or see yourself in a planning or leadership role, you can be sure of a wide ranging of exciting opportunities. The built environment and construction industry in Greater London alone requires an additional 5,200 new recruits every year. This could be your opportunity to shape how our great city develops in the future.
Find out more about Built Environment, Construction and Green Energy careers
Business, Finance, Economics and Marketing
Careers in business help organisations to operate effectively and efficiently, generate income and stay profitable. The engine room of the British economy, job roles in these specialist areas are available in most businesses whether they are small in size or part of multi-national corporate organisations. There are over five million private sector business in the UK employing over 27 million people and new start-ups are launched every year. If you have the ability to think strategically, plan with care and develop your commercial awareness, a career in business could be yours.
Find out more about Business, Finance, Economics and Marketing careers
Creative and Digital Media
Encompassing a wide range of skills and disciplines, the creative and digital sector could see you working in fulfilling roles in advertising, esports, video games design or music. The sector shapes the content we consume every day on our phones, tablets, and PCs, and on radio and television. Make your contribution to this dynamic and exciting industry and you will be working at the forefront of technology and entertainment.
Find out more about careers in Creative and Digital Media
Education
As part of a teaching career, you will be helping to shape the minds and futures of individuals whether they are starting out on their learning journey or returning to education to acquire new skills. As well as teaching your favourite subjects, you will help pupils and students to build their confidence and self-esteem enabling them to fulfil their potential. With opportunities to work in maintained or independent schools, colleges, and universities or as a private tutor, getting qualified in education opens door to a lifelong career in learning. With over 24,000 schools, 270 colleges, and 166 universities in the UK, your skills will always be in demand.
Find out more about careers in Education
Engineering
Engineers are the superheroes solving problems using science, technology, and creativity to make the world a better place. Almost every industry relies on engineers whose designs and creations that benefit society, making systems work and solving problems. With a UK workforce of over eight million, the engineering sector is always keen to recruit passionate and dedicated individuals who are driven by curiosity and a desire to learn how things work.
Find out more about Engineering careers
Health and Social Care
Take your place in the huge team that works to safeguard the nation’s physical and mental health and wellbeing. The health and social care industry is made-up of a huge variety of organisations and agencies focused on our wellbeing with job roles available in hospitals, dental surgeries, care homes, nurseries and in the community. You will need to display the qualities of kindness, empathy, and dedication to succeed in this highly rewarding sector. With strong demand for new entrants, this industry could offer a lifelong career path.
Find out more about Health and Social Care careers
Hospitality, Catering & Tourism
If you have a passion for meeting new people and a talent for providing exceptional service, the hospitality, catering and tourism sector could be the perfect pathway for you. With a wide range of fast-paced and rewarding careers on offer for the right person, the leisure sector is a dynamic and hugely varied industry. With over three million jobs nationally, and half a million in London alone, there is a huge and growing demand for people with service sector skills. If you’re technically competent and have good communication and interpersonal skills, you can be sure of an exciting future.
Find out more about Hospitality, Catering and Tourism careers
IT
The growth of Artificial Intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and digitalisation are just a few of the exciting IT-driven developments that are increasingly shaping our world. Careers in the fast-paced and dynamic world of IT are limitless, and most businesses and organisations need qualified individuals to support their everyday operations. You might work to protect hardware and software infrastructures, become a software developer or systems analyst, or specialise in forensics or geospatial technology. The right qualifications will open doors to a myriad of exciting potential pathways.
Find out more about IT careers
The Arts: Performing Arts and Art & Design
The UK arts sector is flourishing and offers a wonderful world of creativity to talented individuals at all levels. With opportunities in performing and visuals arts for film, TV, video, and radio and within the leisure sector, there is no limit to your progression in this exciting sectors. Think laterally and your skills could take you into photography, fashion, or fine art, production, or teaching. There are over two million people working in creative arts in the UK and the sky is the limit with the right qualifications to back up your talent.
Find out more about Arts careers
Sports and Fitness
The UK sports industry is thriving and offers a wide range of exciting opportunities for individuals who are passionate about sport, fitness, and physical activity. From coaching and sports development to fitness, health, leisure, and sports management, there are countless pathways to build a rewarding career. Think beyond the playing field and your skills could take you into teaching, physiotherapy, sports therapy, performance analysis, event management, or the wider health and wellbeing sector. With the sports industry continuing to grow, the opportunities are endless for those with the dedication, talent, and qualifications to succeed.
Find out more about Sports careers

LSBU Group
Our growing family of like-minded institutions offers students a genuine choice between different styles of learning, centred on the needs of each individual. We share a passion to provide excellent, accessible, supportive and flexible education that creates better life chances, from enhanced career outcomes to improved health and wellbeing.
London South Bank University
LSBU is a vibrant university with a ‘can do, go do’ attitude and big ambitions to be London’s top modern university. It has have served south London for over 125 years with a commitment to providing high-quality education to all. The university has strong links to employers, and courses are applied, accredited and offer placement opportunities. It is one of the biggest providers of degree apprenticeships, and it has a growing portfolio of practical courses, ranging from Engineering and the Built Environment to Health, Law, Film and Media and Business.
Support and opportunities
Being part of an exciting educational group means our students have access to incredible support and opportunities. We regularly work with academics from within the university on enhancing our curriculum. Our students have access to excellent facilities, placement opportunities and advice.
We work within LSBU Group to ensure every student is ready for the next step in their lives; whether that be progression within the group, an apprenticeship or degree or full-time employment.

LSBU Group manifesto
LSBU Group believes knowledge has the power to impact the lives of all people, across all sections of society. To make our world more free, fair and open, help our economy grow, and leave no one behind.
Unbound by tradition, we are a leader in technical education. Learning, delivered at all levels and without prejudice, excellent and accessible in equal measure, empowers people of any age and background to achieve success on their terms.
Career-focused pathways across our institutions open up opportunities for an infinitely diverse cohort, and removes the barriers that have historically stood between so many students and their futures. We are redefining what high quality education means.
Rooted in the real world, we are a partner to industry. Research, knowledge exchange and innovation empowers organisations to work smarter, delivering real value, inspiring optimism and allowing them to see their own potential.
We work with business leaders to shape our curricula and qualifications, ensuring our learners leave ready for the rigours of work - a brilliant and diverse workforce, fit for the future. We are helping our economy to grow.
Committed to our communities, we serve society with integrity, wherever we are in the world. Access to life-changing opportunities, resources and support empowers individuals to live happier, healthier more fulfilling lives.
We work with governmental and grass-roots organisations to deliver a profound economic and social impact. For more than 125 years we’ve worked to “promote the industrial skill, general knowledge, health and well-being of young men and women”. We will never lose sight of this mission.

Our strategy
Connecting is our ambitious vision for LSBU Group 2030 and beyond. By strengthening pathways, partnerships and student success, we will connect people to opportunity, deliver inclusive growth and power social mobility across London and beyond.
Click to view the full strategy or download it here.
From SBUA to LSBU
Daniel Salazar – Psychology at LSBU
Daniel studied at SBUA for both secondary school and sixth form before progressing to London South Bank University to study Psychology.
During his time at SBUA, he gained valuable experience through industry partnerships, university engagement, and dedicated support from staff, helping him feel confident and prepared for higher education.
Daniel Caseria – Physiotherapy at LSBU
After studying at South Bank University Academy, Daniel progressed to London South Bank University to pursue Physiotherapy.
Through early exposure to university and a strong focus on independent learning, Daniel developed the confidence and discipline needed to transition smoothly into higher education. Today, he is gaining hands-on experience through practical sessions while making the most of student life.
